subproblems.title: C^1 approximation of Lipschitz functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5); reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1 and let f : R^n -> R (R^n = Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) be Lipschitz with constant K in R>=0 (LipschitzWith K f). Then for every epsilon in (0, infinity] (an extended nonnegative real) there is a C^1 function g : R^n -> R (ContDiff R 1 g) such that the Lebesgue measure (volume) of {x : f(x) != g(x)} is less than epsilon. (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (f : Rn n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x} < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:

Its candidate is 4d18f1d64ced18737b95cceccbeb3b1995ce254c; it has no dependencies, and #print axioms gives propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. In the selected parent proof this is the scalar case of Claim A (Part A, steps A1-A5). The proof below copies those steps with Lambda := K. Step 0 is added first: it turns the extended-real tolerance of this statement into the real tolerance used in A1-A5.

Source: Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (C^1 Approximation Theorem) and its printed proof (Rademacher 1.4, Lusin, Egoroff, closed subset, Whitney extension theorem 1.6). The parent keeps two refinements of the printed proof. First, L^n is infinite, so Lusin and Egoroff are applied on bounded pieces, which are then glued by local finiteness. Second, the remainder supremum is taken over all y (not only over y in the Lusin set) and computed on a countable dense set, which makes it Borel.

Lean note. Lusin and Whitney live in SimonGMT modules (Chapter01.Lusin, Chapter02.WhitneyJet, Chapter02.WhitneyExtension) that the frozen contract does not import; a proof file adds these imports, and only the frozen definitions must stay unchanged. The accepted candidate already exists, so this note is informational.

Notation. R^n = Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure L^n = volume. B_r(x) is the closed ball and B^o_r(x) the open ball. For a map f, Df(x) := fderiv R f x (Mathlib's Frechet derivative; it is 0 where f is not differentiable).

Checked tools. These come from the pinned Mathlib and the pinned SimonGMT. All are sorry-free and use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
(Rad) Rademacher. A Lipschitz map between finite-dimensional real spaces is differentiable L^n-a.e. (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). For any map f, the differentiability set is Borel, and x -> Df(x) and x -> Df(x)v are Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv, measurable_fderiv_apply_const). If f is Lambda-Lipschitz, then ||Df(x)|| <= Lambda (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
(Eg) Egorov (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto). Let S be a measurable set of finite measure and h_k strongly measurable real functions with h_k -> h at every point of S. For every tau > 0 there is a measurable t contained in S with measure <= tau such that h_k -> h uniformly on S minus t.
(Lu) Lusin (SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable). Let nu be a measure on R^d such that every measurable set S with nu(S) < infinity contains, for every tau > 0, a closed F with nu(S minus F) < tau. If A is measurable with nu(A) < infinity, h : R^d -> R is Borel and tau > 0, then there is a closed C contained in A with nu(A minus C) < tau and h restricted to C continuous. Here only nu = L^n is used; its hypothesis holds because Lebesgue measure is weakly regular (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt; the older name MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_diff_lt is a deprecated alias).
(Wh) Whitney (SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney). Let A be a closed subset of R^n, h : R^n -> R and D : R^n -> (R^n ->L[R] R) with HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h D, i.e.
 (W1) ContinuousOn h A;
 (W2) ContinuousOn D A;
 (W3) for every compact K contained in A and every tau > 0 there is delta > 0 with |h(y) - h(x) - D(x)(y - x)| <= tau |y - x| whenever x in K, y in A and |x - y| < delta.
 Then there is g : R^n -> R with ContDiff R 1 g, g = h on A, and HasFDerivAt g (D a) a for every a in A.

Proof. Let n >= 1, K in R>=0, f : R^n -> R with LipschitzWith K f, and epsilon in (0, infinity]. Put Lambda := K, so f is Lambda-Lipschitz.
0. Real tolerance. If epsilon = infinity, put eps := 1. Otherwise 0 < epsilon < infinity; put eps := epsilon.toReal, so that ENNReal.ofReal eps = epsilon. In both cases eps is a positive real number with ENNReal.ofReal eps <= epsilon. Steps A1-A5 construct a closed set A with L^n(R^n minus A) < ENNReal.ofReal eps and a C^1 function g with g = f on A. Then {f != g} is contained in R^n minus A, so L^n({f != g}) < ENNReal.ofReal eps <= epsilon, which is the claim.
A1. Rademacher. Let B := {x : f is differentiable at x} and D := Df. Let e_1, ..., e_n be a basis of R^n and D_i(x) := D(x)e_i. By (Rad):
 - B is Borel and L^n(R^n minus B) = 0;
 - D and each D_i are Borel;
 - ||D(x)|| <= Lambda for all x;
 - f has Frechet derivative D(x) at every x in B.
A2. Remainder functions. For x != y put R(x,y) := |f(y) - f(x) - D(x)(y - x)| / |y - x|, and R(x,x) := 0. Then 0 <= R <= 2 Lambda, since |f(y) - f(x)| <= Lambda |y - x| and |D(x)(y - x)| <= Lambda |y - x|. Fix a countable dense set Q in R^n (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). For k in N and q in Q, let phi_(k,q)(x) := R(x,q) if 0 < |q - x| < 1/(k+1), and phi_(k,q)(x) := 0 otherwise. Let Rsup_k(x) := sup_(q in Q) phi_(k,q)(x), which lies in [0, 2 Lambda].
 (i) Rsup_k is Borel. The set {x : 0 < |q - x| < 1/(k+1)} is Borel. The map x -> R(x,q) is Borel, because f is continuous, D is Borel and (L, v) -> L v is continuous. So each phi_(k,q) is Borel, and a countable supremum of Borel real functions is Borel (Mathlib Measurable.iSup). In particular Rsup_k is strongly measurable.
 (ii) Rsup_k(x) -> 0 for every x in B. Given tau > 0, differentiability at x gives r > 0 with |f(y) - f(x) - D(x)(y - x)| <= (tau/2) |y - x| for |y - x| < r. If 1/(k+1) < r, every phi_(k,q)(x) is either 0 or R(x,q) <= tau/2, so 0 <= Rsup_k(x) <= tau/2 < tau.
 (iii) If 0 < |y - x| < 1/(k+1), then R(x,y) <= Rsup_k(x). Suppose instead Rsup_k(x) < R(x,y). The functions z -> |z - x| and z -> R(x,z) are continuous at y (as y != x). So there is r > 0 such that every z with |z - y| < r satisfies 0 < |z - x| < 1/(k+1) and R(x,z) > Rsup_k(x). Since Q is dense, some q in Q has |q - y| < r, and then Rsup_k(x) >= phi_(k,q)(x) = R(x,q) > Rsup_k(x), a contradiction.
A3. Egoroff and Lusin on bounded pieces. For m in N let S_m := B cap {x : m <= |x| < m + 1}. The S_m are Borel and pairwise disjoint, L^n(S_m) <= L^n(B_(m+1)(0)) < infinity, and B is the union of the S_m. Choose eps_m > 0 with sum_m eps_m < eps (Mathlib ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable). Fix m.
 (a) Egoroff. Apply (Eg) on S_m to Rsup_k -> 0. The convergence holds at every point of S_m, which is contained in B, by A2(ii), and Rsup_k is strongly measurable by A2(i). This gives a Borel t_m contained in S_m with L^n(t_m) <= eps_m/2 such that Rsup_k -> 0 uniformly on S_m minus t_m.
 (b) Lusin. Apply (Lu) with nu = L^n on the Borel set S_m minus t_m, which has finite measure, to the Borel functions D_1, ..., D_n with tolerance eps_m/(2n) each. This gives closed sets C_(m,i) contained in S_m minus t_m with L^n((S_m minus t_m) minus C_(m,i)) < eps_m/(2n) and D_i continuous on C_(m,i).
 (c) Let K_m := C_(m,1) cap ... cap C_(m,n); as n >= 1, K_m is contained in C_(m,1). Then:
 - K_m is closed and contained in S_m minus t_m, hence in B cap {m <= |x| < m + 1}, so K_m is compact;
 - every D_i is continuous on K_m, so D is continuous on K_m: for v = sum_i v_i e_i we have D(x)v = sum_i v_i D_i(x), and a map into the finite-dimensional space of linear maps is continuous on a set iff all its evaluations are (Mathlib continuousOn_clm_apply);
 - Rsup_k -> 0 uniformly on K_m;
 - S_m minus K_m is contained in t_m union the union over i of ((S_m minus t_m) minus C_(m,i)), so L^n(S_m minus K_m) <= eps_m/2 + n eps_m/(2n) = eps_m.
A4. The closed set A := union over m of K_m.
 (a) A is closed. The family (K_m) is locally finite, because the open ball B^o_1(x) meets K_m only if m < |x| + 1. A locally finite union of closed sets is closed (Mathlib LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion).
 (b) L^n(R^n minus A) < eps. If x is not in A, then either x is not in B, or x lies in S_m minus K_m for m = floor(|x|). Hence L^n(R^n minus A) <= L^n(R^n minus B) + sum_m L^n(S_m minus K_m) <= 0 + sum_m eps_m < eps.
 (c) A is contained in B, so f has derivative D(a) at each a in A.
 (d) D is continuous on A. Let a lie in K_m, and let W := the union over j != m of K_j. W is closed, being a locally finite union of closed sets. Also a is not in W, since the K_j lie in the pairwise disjoint shells {j <= |x| < j + 1}. So the complement of W is a neighbourhood of a whose intersection with A is contained in K_m. Thus K_m is a neighbourhood of a relative to A, and continuity of D restricted to K_m at a gives continuity of D restricted to A at a (Mathlib ContinuousWithinAt.mono_of_mem_nhdsWithin).
 (e) Compact-uniform Taylor remainder. Let K be a compact subset of A and tau > 0. Then K is contained in B_(r_K)(0) for some r_K >= 0, so K is contained in K_0 union ... union K_(floor(r_K)), because the points of K_m have norm >= m. By A3(c), Rsup_k -> 0 uniformly on each of these finitely many sets, so there is k with Rsup_k(x) < tau for every x in K. Put delta := 1/(k+1) > 0, and let x in K and y in A with |x - y| < delta. If y = x, both sides of the inequality in (W3) vanish. Otherwise 0 < |y - x| < 1/(k+1), and A2(iii) gives |f(y) - f(x) - D(x)(y - x)| = R(x,y) |y - x| <= Rsup_k(x) |y - x| <= tau |y - x|.
A5. Whitney. By A4, A is closed, and the three hypotheses hold for h := f and D:
 - (W1): f is Lipschitz, hence continuous;
 - (W2): this is A4(d);
 - (W3): this is A4(e).
 That is, HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f D holds. (Wh) gives g in C^1(R^n), i.e. ContDiff R 1 g, with g = f on A (and Dg(a) = D(a) for a in A). Hence {x : f(x) != g(x)} is contained in R^n minus A, which has L^n-measure < eps by A4(b). By step 0, volume {x | f x != g x} < epsilon, and g is C^1. This proves the statement.
proof_key_steps: Reduce the extended-real tolerance epsilon to a real eps > 0 with ENNReal.ofReal eps <= epsilon
Rademacher: f is differentiable off a Borel L^n-null set B; Df and its components are Borel and bounded by K
Borel remainder suprema Rsup_k over a countable dense set: bounded by 2K, tending to 0 on B, and dominating R(x,y) whenever 0 < |y - x| < 1/(k+1)
Egorov for Rsup_k and Lusin for the partial derivatives on the bounded shells S_m give compact K_m with Df continuous, Rsup_k -> 0 uniformly, and L^n(S_m minus K_m) <= eps_m
A = union of the K_m is closed (locally finite) with L^n(R^n minus A) < eps; Df is continuous on A and the Taylor remainder is uniformly small on compacts, so HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f Df holds
Whitney extension gives g in C^1 with g = f on A, so L^n({f != g}) < eps <= epsilon

Then there exist a Borel set Z_0 in R^(n+l) with H^n(Z_0) = 0 and, for k in N, C^1 maps G_k : R^n -> R^(n+l), points c_k in R^n and reals r_k > 0 and sigma_k > 0 such that, for every k: DG_k(b) = fderiv R G_k b is injective for every b in the open ball B^o_(r_k)(c_k); sigma_k |b_1 - b_2| <= |G_k(b_1) - G_k(b_2)| for all b_1, b_2 in B^o_(r_k)(c_k); and M is contained in Z_0 union the union over k of G_k(B^o_(r_k)(c_k)).

Lean note. The critical-image theorem (Chapter02.AreaCritical) is in a SimonGMT module that the frozen contract does not import; a proof file may add that import or reprove it, and only the frozen definitions must stay unchanged. The accepted candidate already exists, so this note is informational.

Notation. R^n = Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with L^n = volume. R^(n+l) = Amb n l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)). H^n := muHE[n] on every Euclidean space; on R^n, H^n = L^n (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, as finrank R^n = n). B_r(b) is the closed ball and B^o_r(b) the open ball. For a map G, DG(v) := fderiv R G v.

Tools. Apart from the sibling, these come from the pinned Mathlib and SimonGMT; all are sorry-free and use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
(C1A) The sibling c1_approximation (Submission.aetp_lipschitz_c1_approximation). For n >= 1, every Lipschitz h : R^n -> R (LipschitzWith K h for some K in R>=0) and every epsilon in (0, infinity] there is a C^1 function g : R^n -> R with L^n({h != g}) < epsilon.
(AF-i) Critical images (SimonGMT Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). For every map G : R^n -> R^N, H^n(G({v : G is differentiable at v and DG(v) is not injective})) = 0.
(AF-iii) Lipschitz images (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). A K-Lipschitz map on a set A multiplies H^n(A) by at most K^n. In particular, Lipschitz maps send L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets.
(MVI) Mean value inequality (Mathlib Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le). If phi is differentiable on a convex set S and ||Dphi(v)|| <= C for v in S, then |phi(v) - phi(v')| <= C |v - v'| for v, v' in S.
(Lin) Lindelof (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). In a second countable space, every family of open sets has a countable subfamily with the same union.
(Hull) Measurable hull (Mathlib toMeasurable, measurableSet_toMeasurable, subset_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable). For every set S, toMeasurable H^n S is measurable, contains S, and has the same H^n-measure as S. The measurable sets of R^(n+l) are exactly its Borel sets.

Proof. Let n >= 1, l >= 0 and let M be a subset of R^(n+l) with CountablyRectifiable n M.
1. Vector-valued C^1 approximation (parent A6). Let F : R^n -> R^(n+l) be Lambda-Lipschitz and eps > 0 real. Put N' := n + l; then N' >= 1 since n >= 1. Each coordinate F^q(x) := F(x)_q (q in Fin N') is Lambda-Lipschitz, since |F(x)_q - F(y)_q| <= |F(x) - F(y)| (Mathlib PiLp.norm_apply_le). By (C1A) with tolerance ENNReal.ofReal(eps/N') > 0 there are C^1 functions g^q : R^n -> R with L^n({F^q != g^q}) < eps/N'. Let G(x) be the point of R^(n+l) with coordinates g^q(x). G is C^1 because all its coordinates are (Mathlib contDiff_euclidean). If F(x) != G(x), then F^q(x) != g^q(x) for some q. Therefore {F != G} is contained in the union over q of {F^q != g^q}, and L^n({F != G}) <= sum_q L^n({F^q != g^q}) < N' (eps/N') = eps, as a finite sum of N' >= 1 terms that are each < eps/N'.
2. The sets Z_j (parent B1). By hypothesis (CountablyRectifiable n M) there are M_0 with H^n(M_0) = 0 and maps F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) (j in N), F_j being K_j-Lipschitz for some K_j in R>=0, with M contained in M_0 union the union over j of F_j(R^n). For all j in N and i >= 1, step 1 (with eps = 1/i) gives a C^1 map G_ij : R^n -> R^(n+l) with L^n({F_j != G_ij}) < 1/i. Then Z_j := the intersection over i >= 1 of {F_j != G_ij} has L^n(Z_j) <= 1/i for every i, so L^n(Z_j) = 0. By (AF-iii) and H^n = L^n on R^n, H^n(F_j(Z_j)) <= K_j^n L^n(Z_j) = 0. Every v not in Z_j satisfies F_j(v) = G_ij(v) for some i >= 1.
3. Charts of one C^1 map (parent B2). Fix j in N and i >= 1, write G := G_ij, and let O := O_ij := {v : DG(v) is injective}.
 (a) O is open. Let DG(u) be injective. As n >= 1, the unit sphere of R^n is nonempty and compact, so c_u := min over |w| = 1 of |DG(u)w| exists, and c_u > 0. Then |DG(u)w| >= c_u |w| for all w. Every linear map L with ||L - DG(u)|| < c_u is injective, since |Lw| >= (c_u - ||L - DG(u)||) |w|. Finally DG is continuous, as G is C^1 (Mathlib ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), so {v : ||DG(v) - DG(u)|| < c_u} is an open neighbourhood of u contained in O.
 (b) G(R^n minus O) is H^n-null. This is (AF-i): G is differentiable everywhere, so R^n minus O is exactly {v : G is differentiable at v and DG(v) is not injective}.
 (c) Local lower bound. For u in O choose s_u > 0 with B_(s_u)(u) contained in O and ||DG(v) - DG(u)|| <= c_u/2 for |v - u| <= s_u; this is possible because O is open and DG is continuous at u. Apply (MVI) to phi(v) := G(v) - DG(u)v on the convex closed ball B_(s_u)(u). phi is differentiable with Dphi(v) = DG(v) - DG(u), of norm <= c_u/2, so |G(v) - G(v') - DG(u)(v - v')| <= (c_u/2) |v - v'|. Hence |G(v) - G(v')| >= |DG(u)(v - v')| - (c_u/2) |v - v'| >= (c_u/2) |v - v'| for all v, v' in B_(s_u)(u), in particular for all v, v' in B^o_(s_u)(u). Moreover DG(v) is injective for every v in B^o_(s_u)(u), since B^o_(s_u)(u) is contained in O.
 (d) Countably many balls. Every u in O lies in the open ball B^o_(s_u)(u), which is contained in O, so these balls (u in O) have union O. R^n is second countable, so by (Lin) there is a countable set U_ij of points of O with O = the union over u in U_ij of B^o_(s_u)(u).
4. Enumeration with a nondegenerate padding chart (parent B3, change (2)). The set I of triples (j, i, u) with j in N, i >= 1 and u in U_ij is countable, being a countable union of countable sets. Hence I union {*}, where * is an extra padding symbol, is countable and nonempty, and there is a surjection k -> iota(k) from N onto it.
 - If iota(k) = (j, i, u), put G_k := G_ij, c_k := u, r_k := s_u and sigma_k := c_u/2.
 - If iota(k) = *, put G_k := E, c_k := 0, r_k := 1 and sigma_k := 1. Here E : R^n -> R^(n+l) sends v to the point whose first n coordinates are those of v and whose last l coordinates are 0. E is linear, hence C^1 with DE(b) = E for every b. Also |E(v)|^2 = sum_i v_i^2 = |v|^2, so E is injective and |E(b_1) - E(b_2)| = |E(b_1 - b_2)| = |b_1 - b_2|.
 By step 3(c) and these properties of E, for every k:
 - G_k is C^1, r_k > 0 and sigma_k > 0;
 - DG_k(b) is injective for every b in B^o_(r_k)(c_k);
 - sigma_k |b_1 - b_2| <= |G_k(b_1) - G_k(b_2)| for all b_1, b_2 in B^o_(r_k)(c_k).
5. The Borel null set (parent B3, change (1)). Let N_ex := M_0 union (the union over j of F_j(Z_j)) union (the union over (j, i) of G_ij(R^n minus O_ij)). It is a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 2 and 3(b)), so H^n(N_ex) = 0 by countable subadditivity. Put Z_0 := toMeasurable H^n N_ex. By (Hull), Z_0 is a Borel (measurable) set, N_ex is contained in Z_0, and H^n(Z_0) = H^n(N_ex) = 0.
6. Covering (parent B3). Let x in M. By step 2, either x is in M_0, or x = F_j(v) for some j and v.
 - If x is in M_0, then x is in N_ex, hence in Z_0.
 - If x = F_j(v) with v in Z_j, then x is in F_j(Z_j), hence in Z_0.
 - Otherwise x = F_j(v) = G_ij(v) for some i >= 1 (step 2). If v is not in O_ij, then x is in G_ij(R^n minus O_ij), hence in Z_0.
 - Otherwise v is in O_ij, so by step 3(d) v lies in B^o_(s_u)(u) for some u in U_ij. Choose k with iota(k) = (j, i, u), which exists because iota is surjective. Then G_k = G_ij, c_k = u, r_k = s_u, and x = G_k(v) with v in B^o_(r_k)(c_k).
 Hence M is contained in Z_0 union the union over k of G_k(B^o_(r_k)(c_k)).
7. Conclusion. Z_0 is Borel with H^n(Z_0) = 0 (step 5). The data (G_k, c_k, r_k, sigma_k), k in N, have all the stated chart properties (step 4), and the covering holds (step 6). This proves the statement.
proof_key_steps: Coordinatewise application of the sibling c1_approximation: every Lipschitz F : R^n -> R^(n+l) agrees with a C^1 map off a set of L^n-measure < eps
Unpack CountablyRectifiable; choose C^1 maps G_ij with L^n({F_j != G_ij}) < 1/i; Z_j is L^n-null and H^n(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 by the Lipschitz image bound
O_ij = {DG_ij injective} is open, and G_ij(R^n minus O_ij) is H^n-null by the critical-image theorem
The mean value inequality gives an injective derivative and the lower bound (c_u/2)|v - v'| on small balls B^o_(s_u)(u) contained in O_ij; Lindelof gives countably many such balls covering O_ij
Enumerate the countable charts, padding with the linear isometric embedding on the unit ball so that r_k > 0
Take the Borel null hull Z_0 = toMeasurable of the H^n-null exceptional union; a case analysis shows M is contained in Z_0 union the chart images

subproblems.title: Borel, finite-measure bi-Lipschitz C^1 chart image with approximate tangent planes and a continuous projection field (Simon Ch. 3, Thm 1.6 for one C^1 piece); reused accepted declaration
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1 and l >= 0 be natural numbers, R^n = Rn n, R^(n+l) = Amb n l, H^n = muHE[n]. Let G : R^n -> R^(n+l) be a C^1 map, c in R^n, rho in R, kappa > 0, and B' := B^o_rho(c) the open ball. Assume DG(v) = fderiv R G v is injective for every v in B', and kappa |v - w| <= |G(v) - G(w)| for all v, w in B'. Let N := G(B'). Then N is Borel measurable, H^n(N) < infinity, and there is a map T from R^(n+l) to the linear subspaces of R^(n+l) with two properties. First, x -> (T x).starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto T(x), is continuous on N for the operator-norm topology. Second, for every x in N, T(x) is an approximate tangent space of N at x in the sense of SimonGMT Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (T x). That is, finrank T(x) = n and, for every continuous compactly supported f : R^(n+l) -> R, the integral of f over blowUpMap x r '' N tends to the integral of f over T(x), both with respect to H^n, as r -> 0+.

Lean note. Several tools below live in SimonGMT modules that the frozen contract does not import: Chapter02.WeightedArea, Chapter02.AreaLinearWeighted, Chapter02.AreaApproximation, Chapter02.Area, Chapter03.SubmanifoldCover and Chapter04.TangentDensity/WeightedBlowUp. A proof file adds these imports, and only the frozen definitions must stay unchanged. The accepted candidate already exists, so this note is informational.

Notation. R^n = Rn n with L^n = volume. R^(n+l) = Amb n l. H^n := muHE[n] on every Euclidean space; on R^n, H^n = L^n (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). B_r(x) is the closed ball and B^o_r(x) the open ball. eta_(x,r)(z) := r^-1 (z - x) is SimonGMT blowUpMap x r. For a subspace T, p_T := T.starProjection. DG(v) := fderiv R G v. JG(v) := areaJacobianAt G v = normDet(DG(v)) = (det(DG(v)^* DG(v)))^(1/2) (SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet). C_c is the space of continuous, compactly supported f : R^(n+l) -> R.

Checked tools. These come from the pinned Mathlib and the pinned SimonGMT. All are sorry-free and use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
(S) Scaling. eta_(x,r) is a similarity with ratio 1/r, so H^n(eta_(x,r)(E)) = r^-n H^n(E) (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_homothety_image and isometry invariance). Equivalently, the image of H^n restricted to E under eta_(x,r) is r^n times H^n restricted to eta_(x,r)(E). Hence integral_(eta_(x,r)(E)) h dH^n = r^-n integral_E h((z - x)/r) dH^n(z) for H^n-measurable E and measurable h >= 0. For signed h, h is integrable on eta_(x,r)(E) iff z -> h((z - x)/r) is integrable on E, and then the same identity holds.
(AF-ii) Area formula (SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative, a lintegral identity with ofReal(JG)). Let s be a Borel subset of R^n, and let G be differentiable at every point of s, with injective derivative there, and injective on s. Then integral_(G(s)) h dH^n = integral_s JG(v) h(G(v)) dv for every Borel h : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity].
(AF-iii) Lipschitz images (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). A K-Lipschitz map on a set A multiplies H^n(A) by at most K^n.
(LinA) Linear area formula (SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_linear_area_formula). For an injective linear map L : R^n -> R^(n+l), a Borel set A in R^n and g : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity], integral_(L(A)) g dH^n = ofReal(normDet L) integral_A g(L w) dw. For A = R^n, L(A) is the range of L.
(JC) Continuity of the Jacobian (SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet). L -> normDet L is continuous on R^n ->L[R] R^(n+l). Hence, if G is C^1, then v -> JG(v) = normDet(DG(v)) is continuous.
(Sc) Affine change of variables on R^n. For r > 0, u in R^n and Borel g : R^n -> [0, infinity], integral g(u + r w) dw = r^-n integral g(v) dv. This follows from translation invariance of L^n and L^n(rE) = r^n L^n(E) (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_smul, Measure.map_addHaar_smul).
(DCT) Dominated convergence along a countably generated filter (Mathlib MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence). The filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 in R is countably generated.
(MVI) Mean value inequality (Mathlib Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le). If G is differentiable on a convex set S and ||DG(v)|| <= C for v in S, then G is C-Lipschitz on S.
(Inv) Inversion (Mathlib NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). In the complete normed ring R^n ->L[R] R^n, the map A -> Ring.inverse A is continuous at every invertible A.
Bochner forms that make the reduction to f >= 0 in step 5(a) unnecessary are also available: SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (under the hypotheses of (AF-ii), integral_(G(s)) g dH^n = integral_s JG(v) g(G(v)) dv for every g), Chapter02.measurePreserving_linearMap_normDet_smul, and Chapter04.map_inverse_blowUp_carrier with Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_image (the exact form of (S)). Either route proves step 5.

Proof. Let n >= 1, l >= 0, G : R^n -> R^(n+l) of class C^1, c in R^n, rho in R and kappa > 0. Put B' := B^o_rho(c) and N := G(B'). Assume DG(v) is injective for every v in B', and kappa |v - w| <= |G(v) - G(w)| for all v, w in B'.
0. Trivial case. If rho <= 0, then B' and N are empty. Then N is Borel with H^n(N) = 0 < infinity, and the constant map T(x) := {0} works: continuity on the empty set and the tangent condition for points of the empty set are vacuous. Assume rho > 0 from now on.
1. Inverse chart (parent B4). G is injective on B': if v, v' are in B' and G(v) = G(v'), then kappa |v - v'| <= 0, so v = v'. Let psi := Function.invFunOn G B' : R^(n+l) -> R^n. For x in N, psi(x) is in B' and G(psi(x)) = x; and psi(G(v)) = v for v in B'. For x, x' in N, |psi(x) - psi(x')| <= kappa^-1 |G(psi(x)) - G(psi(x'))| = kappa^-1 |x - x'|. So psi is (1/kappa)-Lipschitz on N. In particular psi is continuous on N and maps N into B'.
2. N is Borel (parent B4). B' is the union over m in N of the closed balls B_(rho - 1/(m+1))(c), which are empty when rho - 1/(m+1) < 0: if |v - c| < rho, then |v - c| <= rho - 1/(m+1) for all large m. Each closed ball is compact, as R^n is proper, and G is continuous. So N = G(B') is the union over m of the compact, hence closed, sets G(B_(rho - 1/(m+1))(c)), and N is Borel. (Equivalently, SimonGMT Chapter03.measurableSet_of_isSigmaCompact_borel.)
3. H^n(N) < infinity (parent B4). The closed ball B_rho(c) contains B' and is compact, and DG is continuous because G is C^1 (Mathlib ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). So there is Lambda >= 0 with ||DG(v)|| <= Lambda for v in B_rho(c). As B' is convex and G is differentiable, (MVI) shows that G is Lambda-Lipschitz on B'. By (AF-iii), H^n(N) <= Lambda^n H^n(B') = Lambda^n L^n(B') < infinity, since B' is bounded.
4. Definition of T (parent C0). For every x in R^(n+l) put T(x) := LinearMap.range (DG(psi(x))).toLinearMap = DG(psi(x))(R^n). For x in N this is the tangent plane of N at x; the values for x not in N are irrelevant, since the conclusions about T only concern x in N. For x in N, DG(psi(x)) is injective because psi(x) is in B', so finrank T(x) = finrank R^n = n (Mathlib LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj).
5. Blow-ups (parent C1). Claim: for every x in N and f in C_c, integral_(eta_(x,r)(N)) f dH^n -> integral_(T(x)) f dH^n as r -> 0+. Fix x in N and f in C_c, and let b := psi(x). Then b is in B', x = G(b) and T(x) = DG(b)(R^n). Put L := DG(b).
 (a) Reduction to f >= 0. Write f = f^+ - f^-, where f^+ := max(f, 0) and f^- := max(-f, 0) are nonnegative functions in C_c. All the integrals involved are finite.
 - For r > 0, H^n(eta_(x,r)(N)) = r^-n H^n(N) < infinity by (S) and step 3, and f is bounded and continuous, so f is integrable on eta_(x,r)(N).
 - L is injective, so |Lw| >= c |w| for some c > 0 and every w (as in a linear injective map on the finite-dimensional space R^n: c := min over |w| = 1 of |Lw| > 0). Hence L^-1(K) is bounded for every compact K. By (LinA) with g = the indicator of K, H^n(T(x) cap K) = ofReal(normDet L) L^n(L^-1(K)) < infinity. Taking for K a compact set outside which f vanishes, f is integrable on T(x), since f is bounded.
 Both sides of the claim are therefore linear in f, and it suffices to prove the claim for f >= 0. Assume this from now on.

6. (PC) Projections onto ranges of injective maps. Let A : R^n -> R^(n+l) be an injective continuous linear map and A^* its adjoint. The Gram operator A^*A : R^n -> R^n satisfies <A^*A h, h> = |A h|^2 > 0 for h != 0, so it is injective, hence invertible since R^n is finite-dimensional. Put P(A) := A (A^*A)^-1 A^*. For y in R^(n+l), P(A)y lies in range A, and for every h in R^n, <y - P(A)y, A h> = <A^*y - A^*A (A^*A)^-1 A^*y, h> = 0. So y - P(A)y is orthogonal to range A. The orthogonal projection onto a closed (here finite-dimensional) subspace K is the unique map p with p(y) in K and y - p(y) orthogonal to K for all y. Hence P(A) = p_(range A) = (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).starProjection. The maps A -> A^* (a linear isometry) and the composition of continuous linear maps are continuous. By (Inv), A -> Ring.inverse(A^*A) is continuous at every A for which A^*A is invertible. Hence A -> A Ring.inverse(A^*A) A^* is continuous at every injective A, and it agrees with A -> p_(range A) on the set of injective A. Therefore A -> (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).starProjection is continuous, for the operator-norm topologies, on the set {A : R^n ->L[R] R^(n+l) | A injective}.

8. Conclusion. N = G(B') is Borel (step 2) and H^n(N) < infinity (step 3). The map T of step 4 satisfies: x -> (T x).starProjection is continuous on N (step 7), and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (T x) for every x in N (steps 4 and 5). In the trivial case rho <= 0, step 0 gives the same conclusions. This proves the statement.
